sec: snGFR note, clearance & cystatin C · p737

items.q: The order of arrows in the hyperfiltration note on this page is:
opts: ↑ snGFR → intraglomerular HTN → proteinuria → interstitial fibrosis → ↓ GFR
↑ snGFR → proteinuria → intraglomerular HTN → ↓ GFR → fibrosis
items.exp: GFR = snGFR × number of nephrons; when nephron number falls, snGFR rises to maintain GFR (hyperfiltration injury) → beyond point of compensation → intraglomerular HTN → proteinuria → interstitial fibrosis → ↓ GFR. (Book p737)

items.q: Fill up: The label written on the arrow between the compensatory rise in snGFR and intraglomerular hypertension is 'Beyond point of ______'.
items.exp: The vertical arrow in the note is captioned 'Beyond point of compensation', after which intraglomerular HTN follows. (Book p737)

items.q: Every statement about cystatin C matches the page EXCEPT:
opts: It is filtered and then secreted by the tubule
It is a 13 kDa molecule protein
It is a cysteine protease inhibitor
It is produced at a constant rate by all nucleated cells
items.exp: The bullets read: filtered but not secreted, reabsorbed by PCT; the other three lines are printed as such. (Book p737)

items.q: Cystatin C is reabsorbed by the proximal convoluted tubule but is not secreted by it.
opts: True — both handling lines appear under the cystatin C heading
False — it is secreted by the PCT and not reabsorbed
False — it is neither filtered nor reabsorbed
True — and for that reason it replaces creatinine as the marker
items.exp: The two right-hand bullets state 'Filtered but not secreted' and 'Reabsorbed by PCT'; the page nevertheless ends with 'cannot replace Cr'. (Book p737)

items.q: A 70-year-old amputee on long-term steroids for asthma needs a GFR estimate. Applying this page, ordering cystatin C is best described as:
opts: Useful for the muscle-mass problem, but steroids raise it non-specifically
Ideal, since cystatin C is unaffected by drug therapy
Pointless, since cystatin C also depends on muscle mass
Equivalent to creatinine, which is unaffected by amputation
items.exp: Advantages: not affected by race, diet, muscle mass or drugs; disadvantages: non-specifically elevated in inflammation, taking steroids and smokers — hence it cannot replace creatinine. (Book p737)

items.q: Fill up: Endogenous creatinine clearance is written on this page as U_cr × V divided by ______.
items.exp: Endogenous Cr clearance = (U_cr × V) / P_cr, the generic clearance formula applied to creatinine. (Book p737)

items.q: In the clearance formula printed here, V stands for:
opts: Volume of urine in ml/24 h
items.exp: Clearance = urine concentration × volume of urine in ml/min (V) ÷ plasma concentration. (Book p737)

items.q: Match each cystatin C property with the consequence the page draws from it — 1) Constant production by all nucleated cells 2) Filtered, not secreted, reabsorbed by PCT 3) Raised in inflammation, steroids and smokers … A) Non-specific elevation, so it cannot replace creatinine B) Independent of muscle mass and diet C) Its clearance reflects GFR rather than tubular handling
items.exp: Constant nucleated-cell production is what frees it from the muscle-mass and diet dependence of creatinine; being filtered without secretion makes it a GFR marker; the non-specific elevations are why the page says it cannot replace Cr. (Book p737)

items.q: Cystatin C is explicitly listed as NOT affected by all of the following EXCEPT:
items.exp: The 'Not affected by' block lists race, diet, muscle mass and drugs; inflammation is in the 'Non specifically elevated in' block instead, along with taking steroids and smoking. (Book p737)
